q: What is FoxTerm and what core features does it offer?
answer: FoxTerm is an all-in-one, privacy-first server management application built natively for macOS and iOS. It unifies high-performance

q: What is the difference between the free version and Pro? How does the App Store edition work across devices?
answer: The free version is not a crippled demo — every capability, from the
management, is fully unlocked. The only limit is the number of

you can manage. Subscribing to FoxTerm Pro removes that cap for unlimited nodes; the App Store edition (macOS + iOS) unlocks both macOS and iOS/iPadOS clients simultaneously under the same Apple ID via Universal Purchase, with encrypted configuration sync via your personal iCloud container. q: Which platforms and operating systems are supported?
answer: FoxTerm is built natively for Apple platforms: it runs on macOS 14.0 or later and iOS/iPadOS 17.0 or later, including iPhone and iPad, with a single Universal Purchase unlocking every device. There is no Windows, Android, or Linux desktop build — FoxTerm is engineered exclusively for the native Apple stack.

q: Which protocols and authentication methods are supported?
answer: FoxTerm supports SSH, SFTP, and VNC connections, and manages Docker and Podman engines over SSH. It ships with modern ciphers and key types such as Ed25519, split-pane terminal sessions, command snippets, drag-and-drop SFTP transfers, and visual management of containers, images, and volumes.

q: Does FoxTerm collect data or route my connections through its servers?
answer: No. FoxTerm connects directly from your device to your own servers and never proxies your traffic. It enforces a strict zero-telemetry policy — no analytics, no activity tracking, and no connection logs. Credentials and private keys are encrypted on-device and isolated inside Apple Keychain and Secure Enclave.

title: Software should be
fast, private, and built to last.
lede: Two apps, one standard. FoxTerm is a native terminal client for macOS and iOS; UChat AI is a native AI chat app for Mac, iPhone and iPad. Both are written in Swift, with no Electron, no web wrappers and no telemetry.

label: 01 / WHY FOXTERM
title: The tools weren't good enough. So I wrote one.
body: SSH is the interface infrastructure runs on. It's where late-night deploys happen, where servers get debugged, where things get fixed. Every client I tried either felt stuck in 2004 or charged a subscription for features that should be native.

FoxTerm started as a personal tool — a terminal client that actually respects the macOS and iOS design language, runs on native frameworks, and doesn't phone home. It turned into something worth sharing.
No telemetry. No accounts. No feature gates hiding behind paywalls. Just a tool that does the job and gets out of your way.

label: 02 / ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
title: What FoxTerm is built on — and what it will never compromise.
body: Swift and C — not Electron, not a web wrapper. FoxTerm talks directly to AppKit and UIKit, so it feels like it was born on your Mac and iPhone, not ported from a browser tab.
Zero telemetry. Connection data, keys, and session history never leave the device. Keys live in the Secure Enclave when available — not on a cloud server somewhere.
Cold launch under 400 ms. Terminal rendering at native frame rates. No JavaScript engine overhead, no startup splash screens, no artificial delays.
Free to download with all features included. Pro removes the node limit — via App Store subscription or a one-time activation code. No locked-out essentials, no artificial tiers.

title: Our Commitment: Zero Telemetry
body: FoxTerm is built on the principle that your server infrastructure, credentials, and workflows belong exclusively to you. We operate under a strict
and do not collect, transmit, or store any of your operational data on external servers.
zero-telemetry policy

title: 1. Data We Collect
body: FoxTerm collects absolutely no telemetry data. Specifically:
items: No analytics, usage tracking, or behavior monitoring
No crash reports sent to third-party servers by default
No connection logs, command history, or session metadata
No IP addresses, hostnames, or server fingerprints transmitted

title: Each provider gets its own adapter
body: Anthropic speaks the Messages API, Gemini uses generateContent, Ollama talks to /api/chat, and local GGUF runs in-process through llama.cpp with no HTTP at all. Aggregators such as OpenRouter, Together AI and Replicate get their own credential scopes and model IDs, while Azure deployments and MiniMax's international and China endpoints are handled separately. Model lists, thinking and image-generation capabilities, and default parameters are detected per provider. OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints are an extra option for self-hosted services — not a single pipe that every model is forced through.
